sections.title: Read and apply
sections.purpose: Primary documentation and research consulted on 23 September 2026. Living documentation may change; versioned sources below name their reference release. These references support the technic

sections.title: R01 — C++ Core Guidelines
sections.purpose: Bjarne Stroustrup, Herb Sutter, and contributors. Ownership, interfaces, resource safety, and error-handling guidance. Guidelines are recommendations, not a replacement for the selected lang

sections.title: R02 — Working Draft: Coroutine definitions
sections.purpose: ISO C++ working draft. Language-level coroutine transformation and lifetime rules. This living draft may contain revisions beyond the C++20 baseline used by the companion.

sections.title: R03 — Asynchronous operations
sections.purpose: Boost.Asio documentation. Asynchronous operation and completion model. Framework discussion is separate from the companion’s own Linux poll reactor.

sections.title: R04 — Strands: Use Threads Without Explicit Locking
sections.purpose: Boost.Asio documentation. Serializing handler execution within an execution domain. A strand does not synchronize unrelated access outside that domain.

sections.title: R05 — poll(2)
sections.purpose: Linux man-pages project. Readiness notification, event flags, return values, and timeout interpretation for the native transport exercises.

sections.title: R06 — recv(2)
sections.purpose: Linux man-pages project. Receive operations, short reads, EOF, nonblocking behavior, and errors. TCP application framing must be implemented above this interface.

sections.title: R07 — send(2)
sections.purpose: Linux man-pages project. Partial sending, nonblocking errors, and Linux MSG_NOSIGNAL behavior used by the companion.

sections.title: R08 — RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sections.purpose: IETF, 2022. HTTP method semantics and idempotency. The capstone wire protocol is not HTTP; the standard informs the API comparison.

sections.title: R09 — Core concepts, architecture and lifecycle
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. RPC lifecycle, metadata, method shapes, and status. These concepts do not make the optional schema an implemented gRPC service.

sections.title: R10 — Deadlines
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. Client deadlines, propagation, and server-side resource considerations. A deadline is not a rollback transaction.

sections.title: R11 — Cancellation
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. Cancellation notification and application responsibility for stopping ongoing work. Side effects already committed remain application concerns.

sections.title: R12 — Retry
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. Retry policies, attempts, and transport commitment. Application idempotency and durable identity remain separate design obligations.

sections.title: R13 — Custom Name Resolution
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. Resolver and service-configuration responsibilities when endpoints change. The supplied capstone intentionally uses one explicit worker endpoint.

sections.title: R14 — Language Guide: proto3
sections.purpose: Protocol Buffers documentation. Field numbering, defaults, schema evolution, and generated representation. Review selected runtime and compiler releases before integrating the optional schem

sections.title: R15 — Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
sections.purpose: Leslie Lamport, 1978. Original treatment of happened-before and logical clocks. Logical clock ordering is not elapsed time or a complete reconstruction of causality.

sections.title: R16 — In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm: Extended Version
sections.purpose: Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout, 2014. Raft leader election, replicated logs, and safety reasoning. The book’s fencing model is not an implementation or proof of Raft.

sections.title: R17 — Brewer’s Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services
sections.purpose: Seth Gilbert and Nancy Lynch, 2002. Formal assumptions underlying the consistency/availability limitation during partitions. Avoid interpreting it as an unconstrained product-selection sloga

sections.title: R18 — Transaction
sections.purpose: SQLite documentation. BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, transaction modes, and concurrency boundaries used by the store wrapper.

sections.title: R19 — Isolation in SQLite
sections.purpose: SQLite documentation. Connection isolation, serialized writes, and WAL snapshot behavior. Application-level multi-database workflows need additional coordination.

sections.title: R20 — Write-Ahead Logging
sections.purpose: SQLite documentation. WAL files, checkpoints, concurrency, and operational constraints. Copying only a live database’s main file is not the book’s backup procedure.

sections.title: R21 — PRAGMA Statements
sections.purpose: SQLite documentation. Synchronous settings, busy handling, journal configuration, and user_version. Settings must be checked against the installed library and storage assumptions.

sections.title: R22 — SQLite Online Backup API
sections.purpose: SQLite documentation. Supported snapshot-copy mechanism for a live database. Recovery evidence still requires restore and application-level reconciliation tests.

sections.title: R23 — Transaction Isolation
sections.purpose: PostgreSQL documentation, current branch. Comparison of isolation behavior and retry obligations in a different database. This is not a tested PostgreSQL adapter in the companion.

sections.title: R24 — Client-side caching
sections.purpose: Redis documentation. Invalidation and tracking mechanisms. The chapter’s local versioned cache is a separate single-owner model, not a Redis client implementation.

sections.title: R25 — Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms
sections.purpose: RabbitMQ documentation. Independent publication and consumer acknowledgment boundaries, including redelivery. Acknowledgment alone does not transact an external business effect.

sections.title: R26 — Design
sections.purpose: Apache Kafka 4.1 documentation. Versioned reference for log, delivery, and transaction design. Kafka 4.1 is the cited documentation baseline, not a claim about the newest release.

sections.title: R27 — API guarantees
sections.purpose: etcd 3.5 documentation. Versioned coordination-service consistency and durability guarantees. A lease or local fencing token must not be assigned guarantees beyond its authority.

sections.title: R28 — Authentication
sections.purpose: gRPC documentation. Channel and call credentials and authentication mechanisms. The local capstone does not implement these features.

sections.title: R29 — RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security Protocol Version 1.3
sections.purpose: IETF, 2018. TLS 1.3 protocol reference. Application authorization and endpoint identity policy remain distinct from encryption.

sections.title: R30 — Traces
sections.purpose: OpenTelemetry documentation. Trace, span, context, and causality-oriented observability concepts. The book distinguishes conceptual instrumentation from a deployed collector.

sections.title: R31 — Metric and label naming
sections.purpose: Prometheus documentation. Units, naming, and label design. The capstone’s compact diagnostic response is not claimed to be a complete Prometheus exporter.

sections.title: R32 — Handling Overload
sections.purpose: Google, Site Reliability Engineering. Admission, load shedding, queues, and overload interactions. Numerical queueing examples in this book are original stated-assumption calculations.
